name: @castellan/rust
//: Façade so turbo can see the Rust workspace as ONE node in the repo-wide task graph. It carries no dependencies of its own — Cargo owns those. Every script enters cargo through scripts/cargo-env.sh, which runs the lane inside pixi's `shells` environment when that env is present locally (conda-forge gtk/webkit — the two-environment split, decision-13) and against the ambient toolchain otherwise (system gtk, e.g. CI's apt step). cargo-env.sh cds to the repository root before exec'ing, where Cargo reads the workspace Cargo.toml/deny.toml. `--workspace` is load-bearing: it covers the two Tauri app crates under apps/*/src-tauri as well as everything under crates/. Copied from geoquery's @geoquery/rust, with two additions: `codegen`, the task that derives packages/protocol/src/generated from castellan-protocol, and the cargo-env.sh router itself. The test lane is geoquery's shape: `cargo nextest run` for unit/integration suites, then `cargo test --doc` for the doc-tests nextest does not run — both halves routed through scripts/cargo-env.sh.

scripts.lint: ../scripts/cargo-env.sh fmt --all --check && ../scripts/cargo-env.sh clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && ../scripts/cargo-env.sh deny --workspace check bans licenses sources
